legalName: Expunction of a pre-2021 unlawful carrying of a handgun conviction, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.005
primaryReliefTermBasis: 'expunction' is the Texas statutory term and is on profile:terminology.allowedStateTerms. profile:terminology.primaryConsumerTerm is 'expungement' with avoidUniversalExpungementLabel = true; the consumer-facing word may be expungement in participant copy, but the pleading uses the statutory term.
documentTitleFull: PETITION FOR EXPUNCTION OF CRIMINAL RECORDS — PRE-2021 UNLAWFUL CARRYING OF A HANDGUN (TEX. CODE CRIM. PROC. ART. 55A.005)
courtCaptionNote: Token pattern taken verbatim in form from the compiled profile's own sample caption. The cause number is blank: the matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number on filing. {county} is the participant's arrestCounty answer. No specific district court number, judge or clerk is named.
mechanism: A person tried and convicted of an offence committed before 2021-09-01 under Penal Code 46.02(a), as that section existed before that date, is entitled to expunction. This is a mandatory expunction of a conviction arising from the 2021 permitless-carry change, and it runs on the ordinary ex parte petition route at art. 55A.251, or art. 55A.252 where the offence was fine-only. No waiting period is stated.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategy and outputStrategyDeclared 'custom_pleading', compositionMode null and units[] empty: a single-document controlled pleading, not a composed route.

packetSet.components lists four: a required petition (custom_pleading), a required proposed order (custom_pleading), a conditional fee-waiver statement (official_pdf_fill, the Rule 145 Statement of Inability) and required filing-and-local-practice instructions (process_guidance).

No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government; art. 55A.253(a) prescribes the petition's contents instead. This track is additionally absent from every third-party toolkit, so there is no circulating form even to be tempted by.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: A person tried and convicted of an offence committed before 2021-09-01 under Penal Code 46.02(a), as that section existed before that date, is entitled to expunction.
The ordinary ex parte petition route. Filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred.
Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, a justice court or municipal court of record in either county is also available.

Prescribes the required contents of the petition and requires verification. (b) forbids duplicate agencies; (a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately; (c) requires the district clerk's published agency and e-mail list.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.citation: Tex. Penal Code 46.02(a), as it existed before 2021-09-01
primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Unlawful carrying of a handgun. The route reaches convictions under subsection (a) as it read before the 2021 permitless-carry change, and no other subsection.

includeProposedOrderReason: A proposed order is a required custom_pleading component in the registry packet set for this track, and the compiled profile records that 'each petition is accompanied by a proposed Order' and that 'courts will not grant without a complete proposed order'. It is drafted here as a container: it lists the agencies the participant named and directs each to destroy or return the records, and it carries the TRN under art. 55A.301. It states no finding, no date and no judge.
includeCertificateOfServiceReason: The clerk serves under art. 55A.254; the participant does not serve in the ordinary case. The registry records a certificate of service only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly and names no such county, and packetSet.components has no certificate-of-service component.

counselFlags.statement: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified, and the registry records that BOTH a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury ship because 'county practice chooses between them' and an unsworn declaration 'is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others'. No source read for this track names the statute that authorises an unsworn declaration in place of a notarised verification, and no source names a single county that accepts or refuses one. verificationStatute.citation carries art. 55A.253 because that is the article the source cites for the verification requirement itself; unswornDeclarationAuthority.citation is null. This is the same handling the ND config gives its missing verification statute: null, flagged, not invented.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The statutory authority for an unsworn declaration in a Chapter 55A expunction filing, and whether the packet should ship both blocks or a single block chosen per county.

counselFlags.statement: No certificate of service is drafted. The recorded rule is that the CLERK sends the petition and notice of hearing under art. 55A.254 and that 'the participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly'. No source read for this track names a county in which that local practice applies, so there is no sourced trigger condition and none is invented. includeCertificateOfService is false.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Which counties require the filer to serve the attorney representing the state directly, so the conditional certificate of service can be gated on a real fact rather than omitted.

counselFlags.statement: No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this artifact. Article 102.006 was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the ordinary county civil filing fee for an ex parte petition, which is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. The county figure is unresolved and is a recorded release blocker. Separately, whether the $25 per-non-electronic-entity charge applies twice for the same agency — once under art. 55A.254(f) at the petition stage and again under art. 55A.351(b-3) at the order stage — is supported by the text and unconfirmed in practice, and it changes the participant's total by a multiple of the agency count. The compiled profile's '$250-$500 in many counties' figure is expressly disavowed by the registry as no longer reliable and is not reproduced.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The current district-court civil filing fee county by county, and whether the $25 per-paper-entity charge applies once or twice per agency.

counselFlags.statement: Article 55A.253(a) requires the petition to carry the petitioner's date of birth, driver's licence number and social security number, and the petition is public until the order issues. How Harris, Dallas, Bexar, Tarrant and Travis handle sensitive data in a public civil expunction filing is an open release blocker. Every fixture in this artifact leaves dateOfBirth, ssn, driversLicenseNumber, sex and race blank. That is a deliberate conflict with art. 55A.253(a) and it is recorded here rather than resolved: the protected fields must not be prefilled by any pipeline stage, and the county sensitive-data practice must be pulled before the packet can be assembled for filing.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The sensitive-data handling practice in the five largest counties, and the mechanism by which the participant supplies the art. 55A.253(a) identifiers by hand at filing time rather than through the pipeline.

counselFlags.statement: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency; art. 55A.256(c-1) repeats it for the mistaken-identity application. Counsel classified this as a manual completion item AND a generator constraint. The list is assembled from the participant's own answer (agencyList) and the district clerk's published art. 55A.253(c) list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty. No agency is prefilled by LegalEase.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the generator deduplicates the agency list and never emits two entries for divisions of the same agency.

counselFlags.statement: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private entities that compile and disseminate criminal history record information for compensation separately from government agencies. They go on a separate attachment and are never merged into the agency list; merging them breaks both the no-duplicate rule and the service model.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the private-entity attachment is a distinct list and is never merged into the art. 55A.253(a)(8) agency list.

counselFlags.statement: The order must carry the TRN — the incident number on the Texas DPS criminal history — under art. 55A.301. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect the DPS history; the participant obtains it following DPS form CR-63 and supplies the TRN. The TRN field is blank in every fixture.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the TRN reaches the order only as the participant's own confirmed answer and is never derived.

counselFlags.statement: No notice of hearing is drafted. The court sets the hearing not earlier than the 30th day after filing and the clerk gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each listed entity other than central federal depositories; on receipt DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI. The registry records that WHETHER THE CLERK OR THE FILER PREPARES THE NOTICE OF HEARING varies by county and names no county either way. Drafting a notice would guess at both the preparer and the hearing date.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Which counties require the filer rather than the clerk to prepare the notice of hearing.

counselFlags.statement: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product; confirmed 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is a Texas Legal Services Center legal-aid self-help site whose expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are Texas State University training aids. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form. The compiled TX profile still instructs agents to 'use TexasLawHelp's statewide tools to assemble the right forms' — that instruction is superseded and is not followed here.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage fills or delivers a TexasLawHelp, TJCTC or county clerk form on any Texas expunction track.

counselFlags.statement: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government; the Texas Judicial Branch forms index was confirmed on 2026-08-06 to contain none. Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the contents of the petition instead, and that specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable here. Do not reclassify this track as official_pdf_fill because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the track stays classified custom_pleading and that no circulating unofficial PDF is adopted as a form.

counselFlags.statement: The conditional fee-waiver component is the Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs or an Appeal Bond under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, the bilingual statewide form approved by the Supreme Court of Texas in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090 — the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. It is an official form and is not drafted here. Recorded as a mandatory official-form handoff to the official-PDF overlay lane.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the Rule 145 Statement is acquired at its current revision, hashed and field-mapped by the official-PDF overlay lane.

counselFlags.statement: Cause number, court identity, judge name, the attorney representing the state and that attorney's position, filing date, service completion, hearing date and hearing outcome are blank in every fixture and are never prefilled. County, arrest date, arresting agency, offence and case number reach the document only as the participant's own screening answers. The matter is a NEW civil action and receives a NEW cause number, so no cause number can exist before filing.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage populates court identity, prosecutor position, service completion, a hearing date or any outside-party act.

counselFlags.statement: The track's recorded self-help stop conditions are carried into participant copy verbatim in substance: the state opposes the petition or seeks retention under art. 55A.302; the arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes (State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated); a felony from the same transaction is present or arguable; the limitations analysis is contested; any absconding or bail-jumping history (art. 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible and a participant may not self-identify the fact); the arrest may have been made on an art. 42A.751(b) community-supervision violation warrant, which art. 55A.153 bars; venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence were in different counties; immigration consequences; the participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That every stop condition is wired as a screening stop and not merely printed.

counselFlags.statement: Every official source recorded on this track carries sha256 null — the Chapter 55A statute page, S.B. 1667, H.B. 4504, H.B. 16, the Chapter 102 statute page, the Rule 145 Statement of Inability, DPS form CR-63, the DPS Criminal Records Service page and the Texas Judicial Branch forms index. Staleness cannot be detected for any of them. Chapter 55A is a live target: it was recodified effective 2025-01-01 by H.B. 4504, amended by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, and its fee article was replaced effective 2026-01-01.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Capture hashes for all nine official sources before release, and re-read Chapter 55A at each legislative session boundary.

counselFlags.statement: The compiled TX profile is a conversion of a single Agent Training Reference PDF and does not record this article at all. It corroborates the caption form, the ex parte style, the art. 55A.251 venue rule, the required-contents summary, the proposed-order rule and the seven-step filing sequence, and it is used for exactly those. It is stale or superseded on three points that matter: it quotes a '$250-$500' fee range the registry disavows; it directs agents to TexasLawHelp, which the scope restriction forbids; and its bars-to-expunction section states that 'final conviction for the offence (other than a later pardon) — convictions are generally not expungeable', which is directly wrong for art. 55A.005 and incomplete for art. 55A.004.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the TX profile should be regenerated against a corpus that includes Chapter 55A as recodified and amended.

counselFlags.statement: Two facts decide this route and neither may come from memory: the date the offence was committed, which must be before 2021-09-01, and the subsection of Penal Code 46.02 under which the conviction was entered, which must be 46.02(a) as it existed before that date. The registry records both as confirmable only against a certified copy of the judgment from the clerk of the convicting court, and makes 'the offence date or the statutory subsection cannot be confirmed from court records' a self-help stop condition and an exclusion. A wrong subsection defeats the petition.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That offenceDatePre2021 and penalCodeSubsection are gated on the certified judgment and never accepted from recall alone.

counselFlags.statement: This track expunges a CONVICTION, and the compiled TX profile says the opposite in terms. profile:sourceSections[3] (exclusions) lists as the first bar to expunction: 'Final conviction for the offence (other than a later pardon) — convictions are generally not expungeable', and profile:sourceSections[4] (case_outcomes) routes 'Final conviction (most)' to 'No relief except pardon'. Article 55A.005 is a mandatory expunction of a conviction with no pardon involved. The profile is not merely thin here; on this track it is wrong, and any screening built from the profile alone would refuse an entitled participant.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That TX screening does not use the profile's 'convictions are generally not expungeable' rule as a gate, and that the profile is regenerated to carry art. 55A.005.

counselFlags.statement: The registry records that this route 'is missing from the internal reference and from the TexasLawHelp toolkit entirely, which is why a participant is unlikely to know it exists'. That is a discovery problem rather than a drafting problem, and it belongs to whoever owns screening: nobody arrives asking for art. 55A.005 by name. Screening has to reach it from the offence and the date.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening surfaces this route from an unlawful-carry conviction with a pre-2021-09-01 offence date without the participant naming the article.

counselFlags.statement: Article 55A.005 states no waiting period. The offence-date limit — the offence must have been committed before 2021-09-01 — is an eligibility cut-off and not a waiting period, and the packet must not present it as one. The hearing is set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed, which is a court act and is not alleged.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no waiting-period allegation is generated and that the offence-date cut-off is never rendered as an elapsed-time requirement.
